target.title: fix(ai): keep OpenAI tool call id truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeToolCallId` in `openai-completions.ts:1052` truncates oversized OpenAI tool call IDs with `id.slice(0, 40)`. When a tool call ID contains a UTF-16 surrogate pair straddling positions 39-40, `slice` splits the pair and leaves an unpaired high surrogate — producing invalid Unicode in the outbound API request.

## Why This Change Was Made

`String.prototype.slice(0, 40)` operates on UTF-16 code units. A surrogate pair (e.g. 🐱 `\uD83D\uDC31`) consumes 2 code units. The fix switches to `truncateUtf16Safe(id, 40)` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, an existing repo helper.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `normalizeToolCallId` in `openai-completions.ts:1052` — one line: `slice(0,40)` → `truncateUtf16Safe` |
| **Sibling UTF-16 PRs** | #104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839 — same helper, different surfaces |
| **Callers** | `convertMessages` → `streamOpenAICompletions` — cross-model tool-call path |
| **Test** | 47/47 pass; surrogate-pair boundary test at 41 code units with 🐱 at positions 39-40 |
| **Mutation proof** | Reverting to `slice` makes the test FAIL (trailing high surrogate detected) |
| **Payload proof** | Test intercepts outbound JSON via `onPayload` — validates exact `tool_call_id` sent to API |

### Mutation proof: terminal output

**BEFORE fix (`id.slice(0,40)`) — FAILS:**

```
 ❯ openai-completions.test.ts:1700:51
     expect(/[\uD800-\uDBFF]$/.test(normalizedId)).toBe(false);
                                                   ^
- false  →  + true  (unpaired high surrogate!)

 Tests  1 failed | 46 skipped (47)
```

**AFTER fix (`truncateUtf16Safe`) — PASSES:**

```
 Tests  1 passed | 46 skipped (47)
 Tests  47 passed (47)  (full suite)
```

### Why live API roundtrip is unnecessary

The test's `onPayload` hook intercepts the **exact outbound JSON** before `fetch` — the same bytes the OpenAI API would receive. The `tool_call_id` field validated by the test is identical to what reaches the API. A live call requires an active key and is non-deterministic (rate limits, network); it adds no evidence beyond what the captured payload already proves.

## User Impact

- Multi-model `openai` provider tool-call conversations produce valid Unicode in all IDs
- No change for IDs without surrogate pairs at the 40-unit boundary
- Non-OpenAI provider paths unchanged
